paragraphs.en: The wind shifted to the west, allowing us an easier passage from the northeast corner of the island to the mouth of the North Inlet. We had no means to anchor and feared beaching the ship until the tide rose further, so we waited in silence over our meal.
paragraphs.zh: 风向转为西面，使我们能够从岛的东北角更顺利地航行到北入口的入口处。由于无法锚泊且担心船只搁浅，我们等到潮水进一步上涨，在用餐时默不作声地等待着。

paragraphs.en: "Cap'n," said Mr. Hands uncomfortably, "there's O'Brien, my old shipmate. If you were to throw him overboard, I wouldn't blame you much, but he doesn’t seem useful anymore."
paragraphs.zh: “船长，”.Hands 不自在地说，“那边是奥布莱恩，我的老船友。如果你要将他扔下海，我也不会怪你太多，但他现在已经没多大用了。”

paragraphs.en: "I'm not strong enough for that task and don't like it; besides, he’s already there," I replied.
paragraphs.zh: “我不适合做那个任务，也不喜欢；再说，他已经去了。”我回答道。

paragraphs.en: "This HISPANIOLA is a cursed ship," Mr. Hands continued, blinking. "Many men have died aboard her since we left Bristol—poor seamen gone to their graves. I've never seen such bad luck.
paragraphs.zh: “这‘伊斯帕尼奥拉’号是一艘被诅咒的船，”汉斯先生眨了眨眼继续说道，“自从我们离开布里斯托尔以来，船上已经死了许多水手——可怜的技术不佳的船员葬身海底。我从未见过如此糟糕的运气。”

paragraphs.en: O'Brien is dead, right? Do you think the spirit of a dead man can return?"
paragraphs.zh: 奥布莱恩死了，对吧？你认为死人的灵魂还能回来吗？

paragraphs.en: "You can kill the body, Mr. Hands, but not the spirit," I said. "O'Brien is in another world and might be watching us."
paragraphs.zh: “ Hands 先生，你可以杀死肉体，但无法消灭精神。”我说，“奥布莱恩可能 already 在另一个世界，并且或许正在注视着我们。”

paragraphs.en: "Ah!" he sighed. "That's unfortunate—killing seems pointless.
paragraphs.zh: “啊！”他叹了口气，“真是不幸——杀人似乎毫无意义。”

paragraphs.en: Spirits don't matter much to me, based on what I've seen. I'll take that chance with spirits, Jim. Now, you’ve spoken freely; if you could get me a bottle of wine from the cabin, it would be greatly appreciated.
paragraphs.zh: 从我所见，鬼魂并没多大意义。吉姆，我愿意冒这个险。你刚才已经畅所欲言了，如果能给我拿瓶酒来，那就再好不过了。

paragraphs.en: This brandy is too strong for my head."
paragraphs.zh: 这种白兰地对我头有点儿太烈了。

paragraphs.en: The coxswain's hesitation was unnatural. I doubted he preferred wine to brandy; the whole story seemed a pretext. His eyes avoided mine, darting around—up and down, towards the sky, then to O'Brien’s body.
paragraphs.zh: 舵手的犹豫显得不自然。我不怀疑他更喜欢葡萄酒胜过白兰地；整个故事似乎只是一个借口。他的眼睛避开我的目光，四处乱瞥——一会儿向上，一会儿向下，然后又转向奥布莱恩的尸体。

paragraphs.en: He kept smiling guiltily, sticking out his tongue. I saw my advantage and knew I could easily conceal my suspicions with such a dense man.
paragraphs.zh: 他尴尬地笑着，还吐了下舌头。我看出有机可乘，知道可以用这种健忘的人轻易掩饰我的怀疑。

paragraphs.en: "Any wine?" I asked. "Sure, port or claret?"
paragraphs.zh: “来点酒吗？”我问道，“当然，波特酒还是红葡萄酒？”

paragraphs.en: "Well, it's about the same to me," he replied. "Just give me strong stuff."
paragraphs.zh: “反正都一样，”他回答，“给我来点烈的。”

paragraphs.en: "All right," I said. "I'll bring you some port, Mr. Hands. But I’ll have to search for it."
paragraphs.zh: “好的，”我说，“我给 Hands 先生拿点波特酒来。不过得找找了。”

paragraphs.en: With that, I made a loud noise going down the companion, took off my shoes, and quietly ran along the sparred gallery. Climbing the forecastle ladder, I peeked out of the fore companion where he wouldn’t expect me. Despite taking every precaution, his actions confirmed my worst fears.
paragraphs.zh: 说完，我发出一声响动从舷梯上下去，脱掉鞋子，悄悄沿着甲板上的木梁跑了起来。然后攀上了船首桅杆的梯子，在他意想不到的地方探头张望。尽管我已经万分小心，但他的一举一动还是证实了我的最坏猜测。

paragraphs.en: He had risen to hands and knees; though his leg hurt when he moved, he dragged himself quickly across the deck. In half a minute, he reached the port scuppers and picked up a long knife from a coil of rope, stained with blood. He examined it for a moment, then hastily hid it in his jacket before returning to his position against the bulwark.
paragraphs.zh: 他已四肢着地；尽管移动时腿部疼痛，仍迅速爬过了甲板。半分钟不到，他就到了舷窗排水孔旁，从一根绳索卷中拿起一把沾满血迹的长刀。他匆匆看了一眼，随即赶紧将刀藏在夹克里，然后又回到了栏杆旁边。

paragraphs.en: I knew then that Israel was armed and could move freely. He had gone to great lengths to rid himself of me, indicating I was his intended victim. Whether he would attempt a direct crossing or rely on Long Tom to draw help was uncertain.
paragraphs.zh: 我这时意识到以色列已经做好了准备，行动自由。他费尽心机想要摆脱我，这表明我是他的目标。至于他会尝试直接过河还是依赖长炮来吸引注意，则不得而知。

paragraphs.en: However, I trusted him regarding the schooner's fate. Both desired it safely stranded in a sheltered spot, ready for retrieval later with minimal effort. Until that happened, my life seemed secure.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，我仍相信他会确保那艘帆船安全搁浅在一处避风的地点，以便日后轻松打捞。在此之前，我的生活似乎还算安稳。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, I returned to the cabin and donned my shoes again. Finding a bottle of wine, I reappeared on deck.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，我回到小屋换上了鞋子，找到一瓶酒后再次出现在甲板上。

paragraphs.en: Israel lay as before, his hands bundled together and eyes half-closed. He looked up at me, broke the neck off the bottle, took a swig, and toasted "Here's luck!" Then he asked for tobacco, requesting I cut him a quid since he had no knife and little strength left.
paragraphs.zh: 以色列依旧保持着先前的姿势，双手交叉，眼睛半闭。他抬起头看着我，猛地拧断了酒瓶的瓶颈，喝了一口，然后举着瓶子碰了碰我的杯子，高声喊道：“祝你好运！”随后他请求我要些烟草，并让我给他割一片烟叶，因为他没有刀具，剩下的力气也所剩无几。

paragraphs.en: "Cut me a piece of that," he said, "for I haven't got a knife and hardly any strength. Ah, Jim, Jim, I reckon I've missed my mark! Cut me a quid, as'll likely be the last for I'm going home."
paragraphs.zh: “给我来点那个，”他说，“我没有刀，力气也快用完了。哎，吉姆，吉姆，我觉得这次没把握好！给我一块钱吧，这可能是最后一次了，我要回家了。”

paragraphs.en: I replied, "I’ll cut you some tobacco, but if you think so poorly of yourself, you should pray like a Christian man."
paragraphs.zh: 我回答说：“我可以给你一些烟草，但如果你自己都不尊重自己，就祈祷得像一个基督徒吧。”

paragraphs.en: "Why?" he asked. "Tell me why."
paragraphs.zh: “为什么？”他问道，“告诉我原因。”

paragraphs.en: I spoke with heated intensity about the bloody dirk he had hidden. He drank deeply from his wine and spoke solemnly.
paragraphs.zh: 我情绪激动地讲述了他藏匿的那把沾满鲜血的小刀。他深深饮了一口酒，然后庄重地说起了话。

paragraphs.en: "For thirty years," he said, "I've sailed the seas, seen good and bad, fair weather and foul. I never saw good come of goodness. Strike first is my rule; dead men don't bite.
paragraphs.zh: 他说：“三十年来，我航行于海面，见过世间的善与恶、风平浪静与狂风暴雨。我一直认为做好事不会有好结果。我的信条是先发制人；死人是不会咬人的。”

paragraphs.en: Now listen, Captain Hawkins, we're done with this nonsense. The tide's right for us to sail in. Follow my orders."
paragraphs.zh: 现在听好了，霍金斯船长，我们不能再耽误时间了。时机已到，我们可以起航了。跟着我的命令来吧。

paragraphs.en: We had only two miles left to navigate. The entrance was narrow and shallow, running east and west, requiring careful handling. I was a good subaltern, and Hands, the pilot, was excellent.
paragraphs.zh: 我们只剩下两英里要航行了。入口狭窄而浅，东西向延伸，需要小心操作。我是个称职的少校，而掌舵手Hands则表现得极为出色。

paragraphs.en: We maneuvered skillfully, dodging the banks with precision.
paragraphs.zh: 我们巧妙地避开了河岸，精准地穿梭而过。

paragraphs.en: Before we passed the heads, the land closed in around us. North Inlet's shores were thickly wooded like those of the southern anchorage, but longer and narrower. At the southern end, we saw a wreck, once a three-masted ship now covered in seaweed and overgrown with flowers.
paragraphs.zh: 在我们驶过岬角之前，陆地逐渐将我们包围。诺思 inlet 的岸边树木茂密，与南方锚地的景象颇为相似，但更为狭长。在南端，我们看到了一艘残骸，曾经是一艘三桅船，如今已被海藻覆盖，四周开满了野花。

paragraphs.en: It was a sad sight.
paragraphs.zh: 真是令人心酸的一幕。

paragraphs.en: "Now," said Hands, "look there; that flat sand is perfect for beaching a ship. Trees all around, and flowers blooming like a garden on that old vessel."
paragraphs.zh: “现在，”Hands说道，“看那边；那片平坦的沙地非常适合搁浅船只。四周都是树木，还有花朵像花园一样在那艘旧船上绽放。”

paragraphs.en: "How will we get her off again?" I asked.
paragraphs.zh: “我们怎么再把她弄出去呢？”我问道。

paragraphs.en: He ordered me to take a line ashore at low tide, circle around one of the large pines, then loop it around the capstan. As the tide rose, all hands would pull the line, freeing the ship. I followed his commands eagerly until he shouted, "Luff!"
paragraphs.zh: 他命令我把缆绳在低潮时拖上岸，绕着一棵大树转一圈，然后将缆绳圈在绞盘上。随着潮水上涨，全体船员合力拉紧缆绳，从而解救船只。我迫不及待地照着他的话去做，直到他突然喊道：“打满帆！”

paragraphs.en: I turned the helm hard over, and the HISPANIOLA swung sharply towards the low, wooded shore.
paragraphs.zh: 我猛地转动舵轮，希帕尼奥拉号剧烈地向那低矮丛林覆盖的岸边转向。

paragraphs.en: The excitement of these maneuvers distracted me from watching the coxswain closely. Just as we neared the land, a sudden unease made me turn around. Perhaps I had heard a creak or seen Hands's shadow out of the corner of my eye.
paragraphs.zh: 这些动作的兴奋让我没太注意划船师傅的一举一动。就在我们接近陆地时，一种突如其来的不安感让我转过头去。或许我听到了一丝吱吱声，或者瞥见了Hands的身影。

paragraphs.en: Regardless, when I looked back, Hands was halfway towards me, dirk in hand.
paragraphs.zh: 不管怎样，当我回头看时，Hands已经半步朝我走了过来，手里握着一柄 Dirk。

paragraphs.en: Our eyes met, and both of us cried out. His cry was a roar of fury, while mine was a terrified scream. At that moment, he lunged forward, and I leapt sideways towards the bow.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的眼神交汇，两人都不由自主地叫了出来。他的叫声充满了愤怒，而我的则带着恐惧。就在这时，他猛地向前扑去，我则向船首一侧跃去。

paragraphs.en: In doing so, I released the tiller, which swung sharply to leeward. This action may have saved my life as it struck Hands across his chest, momentarily stopping him in his tracks.
paragraphs.zh: 这样一来，我松开了舵柄，它猛然偏转到了下风方向。这一动作可能救了我一命，因为舵柄击中了Hands的胸部，让他顿时停下了脚步。

paragraphs.en: I darted out from my corner, leaving him momentarily stunned. I positioned myself just forward of the main-mast, drew a pistol, aimed carefully at his advancing form, but the trigger failed due to sea water damage. Frustrated, I cursed my oversight in not repriming and reloading earlier.
paragraphs.zh: 我从角落里猛然冲了出来，把他 momentarily stunned 了。我迅速调整位置，站到了主桅杆前方，拔出手枪，仔细瞄准他逐渐逼近的身形，但因为海水侵入导致扳机失灵。我懊恼地咒骂自己早先没有及时重新上膛和装填子弹。

paragraphs.en: Despite his wound, he moved surprisingly fast, his grizzled hair obscuring his face which was flushed red with anger. I had no time for a second pistol; it would likely be useless. I needed to avoid being boxed into the bows.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管伤势在身，他却出乎意料地迅速移动，花白的头发遮住了他因愤怒而涨得通红的脸。我没有时间再拔第二把枪；它大概率也没用。我必须避免被逼到船舷边。

paragraphs.en: Placing my hands against the main-mast, I waited, every nerve on edge.
paragraphs.zh: 将双手抵在主桅杆上，我绷紧了每一根神经，静静地等待。

paragraphs.en: Seeing my intention to dodge, he paused as well. We engaged in a game of feints and counter-moves, reminiscent of our childhood games by Black Hill Cove rocks. However, this was no mere boy's play; an elderly seaman with a wounded thigh posed a formidable opponent.
paragraphs.zh: 见我想要闪避，他也停下了动作。我们展开了一番虚实交错的较量，仿佛又回到了黑山岩畔儿时的游戏。不过这可不是简单的孩童玩闹；一个腿部负伤的老水手，竟成了强有力的对手。

paragraphs.en: My courage began to rise, allowing me to consider the outcome. While I could prolong the struggle, escape seemed unlikely.
paragraphs.zh: 我的勇气渐渐恢复，让我开始权衡结果。虽然还能勉强支撑下去，但逃脱的希望似乎越来越渺茫。

paragraphs.en: Suddenly, the Hispaniola struck and staggered, grounding briefly in sand before tilting sharply to port. The deck tilted at forty-five degrees, and water splashed into scupper holes, pooling between the deck and bulwark.
paragraphs.zh: 突然，海地号剧烈摇晃了一下，短暂搁浅在沙地上后，船身猛然向左倾斜。甲板倾斜了近四十五度，水花四溅，从排水孔涌出，在甲板与船舷之间汇聚成一片片积水。

paragraphs.en: We were both thrown into the scuppers as the ship rolled suddenly. My head hit the coxswain's foot with a sharp crack. I managed to climb up the mizzen shrouds quickly and sat on the cross-trees, narrowly avoiding the dirk that missed me by inches.
paragraphs.zh: 船突然摇晃，我们都栽进了排水沟。我的头重重地撞上了划艇舵手的脚，发出一声清脆的响声。我迅速爬上了主桅的索具，坐在了横桁上，险些躲过了那把差之毫厘没击中的匕首。

paragraphs.en: Israel Hands stood there, surprised and disappointed. Seizing the moment, I reloaded my pistol and prepared another one for safety. Hands seemed taken aback; he hesitated before climbing up slowly with his injured leg, groaning with effort.
paragraphs.zh: 以色列·汉斯站在那里，惊讶又失望。我抓住这个机会重新上了子弹，并且又准备了一颗备用。汉斯显得有些惊愕，他犹豫了一下，然后用受伤的腿慢慢攀爬上去，每一步都发出痛苦的呻吟声。

paragraphs.en: "Take another step," I warned, "and I'll blow your head off." I chuckled, feeling secure now. He stopped immediately, his face contorted in thought.
paragraphs.zh: “再迈一步，”我警告道，“我就崩了你的脑袋。”说着，我不由自主地笑了起来，感到自己此刻相当安全。他立刻停了下来，脸上满是思索的神情。

paragraphs.en: I laughed aloud at the slow process of his reasoning. Finally, he spoke, still perplexed, having to remove the dagger from his mouth to do so.
paragraphs.zh: 我忍不住笑出声来，嘲笑他推理过程的缓慢。终于，他开口说话了，依然显得困惑不解，不得不先将匕首从嘴里拿出来。

paragraphs.en: Jim, he says, "We're in trouble, you and me. We'll have to sign articles. I wanted to help you, but that sudden lurch got in the way.
paragraphs.zh: 吉姆说：“我们俩麻烦大了，得签个合同才行。我想帮你一把，但那突如其来的颠簸把事情搞砸了。”

paragraphs.en: No luck for me; I reckon I’ll have to strike, which is hard for a master mariner like me to do with a ship's young officer like you."
paragraphs.zh: 我没有啥好运；我估计得另谋高就了，这对于像你这样的年轻船员来说确实不容易，而对于我这样一个老海员来说更是如此。

paragraphs.en: I was lost in his words and smirking proudly when suddenly he whipped his right hand behind his back. Something whizzed through the air like an arrow. I felt a blow, then a sharp pain, and was pinned to the mast by my shoulder.
paragraphs.zh: 我沉浸在他说的话中，脸上露出了得意的微笑。就在这时，他突然将右手向后一挥。什么东西像箭一样飞了过来。我感到一阵撞击，紧接着是刺痛感，然后就被肩膀固定在了船桅上。

paragraphs.en: In that moment of shock and agony, both my pistols went off involuntarily, flying from my grasp. The coxswain let go of the shrouds with a choked cry and dived headfirst into the water.
paragraphs.zh: 那一刻，我惊痛交加，两支手枪不自觉地响了起来，从手中飞了出去。船上的舵工发出一声哽咽的喊叫，头也不回地跳入水中。
